question.questionText: She will take the exam, __________ she gets sick.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The blank requires a conjunction that expresses the idea that she will take the exam regardless of whether she gets sick or not. The sentence structure is: 'She will take the exam, __________ she gets sick.' The correct conjunction here is 'even if', which means 'whether or not'.
  • provided that (conjunction): Means 'only if' or 'on the condition that'. It is used to express a condition that must be met for something to happen.
  • while (conjunction): Means 'during the time that' or 'although'. It is used to show contrast or simultaneous actions.
  • even if (conjunction): Means 'whether or not'. It is used to show that the action will happen regardless of the condition.
  • before (conjunction/preposition): Means 'earlier than'. It is used to indicate time.
Related structure or vocabulary: even if + clause: used to express that something will happen regardless of a certain condition.

The blank in the sentence '__________ she had left, he came back home.' requires a conjunction that shows the relationship between the two actions: her leaving and his coming back home. The correct conjunction should indicate that his return happened after she had left.
  • If (Conjunction): Used to express a condition (e.g., If it rains, we will stay home). It does not fit the context of the sentence, which is about the sequence of events.
  • Because (Conjunction): Used to show reason or cause (e.g., He left because he was tired). It does not fit here, as the sentence is not explaining a reason.
  • While (Conjunction): Used to indicate two actions happening at the same time (e.g., She was reading while he was cooking). It does not fit because the two actions did not happen simultaneously.
  • After (Conjunction): Used to show that one action happens following another (e.g., After she finished, he started). This fits the context, as he came back home after she had left.

question.questionText: I had had an outstanding balance of $453 on my account; __________ , I paid off my entire account balance last weekend.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The blank in the sentence requires a transition word that shows the relationship between the two clauses. The first clause states that there was an outstanding balance of $453, and the second clause says that the speaker paid off the entire balance last weekend. The two clauses contrast with each other: having a balance and then paying it off. The correct transition to show this contrast is 'however.'
  • however (conjunction/adverb): Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or seems to contradict something that has been said previously.
  • therefore (conjunction/adverb): Used to introduce a logical result or conclusion from what has just been stated.
  • consequently (adverb): Used to show that the second statement is a result of the first.
  • furthermore (adverb): Used to add information; means 'in addition.'
Related structure or vocabulary: Transition words for contrast: 'however', 'nevertheless', 'on the other hand'. These words are used to show contrast between two ideas.

The blank in the sentence 'Trains in Finland are seldom on schedule _________ they depart on time.' requires a conjunction that shows contrast between two clauses: 'Trains are seldom on schedule' (they are rarely on time) and 'they depart on time' (they leave on time). The correct conjunction to show this contrast is 'although'.
  • when (conjunction): Used to indicate the time at which something happens. It does not show contrast.
  • until (conjunction/preposition): Used to indicate up to the point in time or the event mentioned. It does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
  • although (conjunction): Used to introduce a contrast or unexpected result between two clauses.
  • since (conjunction/preposition): Used to indicate time (from a point in the past) or reason (because). It does not show contrast here.
Related structure or vocabulary: Conjunctions of contrast: although, though, even though. These are used to connect two clauses with contrasting ideas.

question.questionText: We did our utmost _________ we take back the lost documents.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The blank requires a conjunction or phrase that shows purpose or reason. The sentence 'We did our utmost _________ we take back the lost documents.' means that we tried our best with the aim of retrieving the lost documents. The correct connector to express purpose is 'so that'.
  • in spite of (preposition): A preposition used to show contrast, meaning 'despite'. It is not used to express purpose.
  • so that (conjunction): A conjunction used to express purpose, meaning 'in order to'.
  • despite (preposition): A preposition used to show contrast, similar to 'in spite of'. Not used for purpose.
  • though (conjunction): A conjunction used to show contrast, meaning 'although'. Not used for purpose.
Related structure or vocabulary: so that + clause: used to express purpose (We do something so that something else can happen).
question.explanationViHtml:
Giải thích chi tiết:
Chỗ trống cần một liên từ hoặc cụm từ để chỉ mục đích hoặc lý do. Câu 'We did our utmost _________ we take back the lost documents.' có nghĩa là chúng tôi đã cố gắng hết sức với mục đích lấy lại các tài liệu bị mất. Liên từ đúng để diễn đạt mục đích là 'so that'.
  • in spite of (giới từ): Giới từ dùng để chỉ sự tương phản, nghĩa là 'mặc dù'. Không dùng để chỉ mục đích.
  • so that (liên từ): Liên từ dùng để chỉ mục đích, nghĩa là 'để'.
  • despite (giới từ): Giới từ dùng để chỉ sự tương phản, tương tự 'in spite of'. Không dùng để chỉ mục đích.
  • though (liên từ): Liên từ dùng để chỉ sự tương phản, nghĩa là 'mặc dù'. Không dùng để chỉ mục đích.
Cấu trúc và từ vựng: so that + mệnh đề: dùng để chỉ mục đích (Chúng ta làm gì đó để điều gì khác có thể xảy ra).

Tạm dịch: Chúng tôi đã cố gắng hết sức để lấy lại các tài liệu bị mất.
